title: Small, every week
sub: The fourth and last film of Quality as a habit, and the last of the module Data quality: in Mexico, from 1945, a small team of Mexican agronomists and Norman Borlaug beat the wheat's stem rust by growing two generations a year, in two fields far apart, and keeping the best each round; at the university, after 41 certificates were printed again, four people meet for fifteen minutes every Thursday, make one small change, measure it and keep it with a check, and a year later it is 3.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's look, the quality bench: the data team's workroom, a wall of warm limestone over a granite bench, light from a window on the right; records are cream index cards, and results are tags tied on with string. Green is a check that passes, amber a name held for a person to look at, red a check that stops, grey not checked; brass is what good means for a use, and steel blue a measure taken. Mexico's wheat fields are painted in the same light, and the rust's red-brown is the rust's own.
